messages:
Maya (support): ACME reports a p99 spike starting ~2026-03-17 10:40 UTC. p95 ~3x baseline, p99 > 10s. They see 429s and occasional 503s. Customer says nothing changed on their side. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/apps/tenants/ACME/latency

deploy-bot: canary deploy finished: service/inference v3.4.2 @ 2026-03-17T10:39:12Z (canary->stable) :deploy:

Priya (eng-runtime): looking. can you drop a sample request_id + tenant id and a minimal repro curl?

Maya (support): request_id=6f2a9b0c, tenant=acme-prod. Repro steps: 1) POST /v1/generate w/ prompt ~120 tokens at 10rps for 30s. 2) Observe p95/p99. curl: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","input":"test prompt...","max_tokens":120}'
```
We also saw a cluster-level spike in queue length on the tenant-shared pool: attached screenshot (sent privately).

Jorge (sre): pulled metrics for tenant-shared pool at 10:35-10:45. Observed: inflight request count jumped, request queue length spiked, admission drops increased ~30%. Worker CPU/GPU utilization ~95% but no OOMs. Many requests stuck waiting for KV cache warmup -> higher latencies. Looks like backlog (queueing) rather than model slowdown.

Li (oncall): running quick log grep for request_id: `rg "6f2a9b0c" /var/log/inference/* | head` -> found tail of logs showing repeated `AdmitQueue.WaitTimeout` and `AdmissionController.Drop` with reason=concurrency_limit.

Priya (eng-runtime): hmm — v3.4.2 included a change to the tenant admission controller: we tightened per-tenant fairness window to avoid noisy neighbour. That reduces burst concurrency to protect steady throughput, but it can make short bursts wait longer. Could be too strict for ACME's traffic pattern.

Maya (support): customer traffic is bursty (short bursts of many small requests). They rely on fast tails. They are on the shared pool (not dedicated). Any hotfix steps we can do to restore p99 quickly?

Jorge (sre): mitigation options (short term):
- route acme-prod to alternate pool (scale up a fresh pool)
- temporarily increase tenant concurrency cap for acme-prod (admit controller)
- change admit policy to fail-fast for overload (instead of wait) so errors are obvious, avoiding long tails
- if rollback acceptable, revert v3.4.2 admit change (takes longer)

Priya (eng-runtime): I can push a canary admit config bump for acme-prod on shared pool (increase burst window + concurrency by 2x) and watch. I'll also open a rollback PR if bump doesn't help. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/admit-config/pulls/459

Li (oncall): I'll provision an alt pool and route traffic now. Command: `rctl pool create --name alt-shared-01 --gpu-type a10 --size 6 && rctl route add --tenant acme-prod --pool alt-shared-01`

(5m later)
Li (oncall): Alt pool created and routing applied. Real-time graph: p99 dropped from ~12s -> ~1.8s within 30s of routing. p95 back to baseline. Customer confirmed improvement. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): ACME confirmed degraded UX resolved after reroute. They want a follow-up on root cause and permanent options (dedicated pool or config changes).

Priya (eng-runtime): action items:
- revert admit tightness change or tune fairness window for bursty tenants (PR #459 pending testing)
- add a per-tenant burst-detection override to allow short bursts for customers flagged as bursty
- postmortem writeup with timelines + replicable repro in harness

Jorge (sre): I'll also add a metric alarm for queue length + admission drops per-tenant so we detect earlier and auto-scale the alt pool or trigger automated reroute.

Maya (support): passing to CS to offer ACME a dedicated pool quote and document temporary steps we took. Will schedule post-incident review tomorrow.

Priya (eng-runtime): quick note for the runbook: if p99 spike + admission_drop increase + worker util ~95% -> prefer routing to alt pool OR increase tenant concurrency cap before rollback.

Li (oncall): closing the live incident — customer satisfied. Leaving notes and logs in the incident channel + ticket #INC-2026-734.

Maya (support): thanks everyone. We'll follow up with postmortem and customer communication. :white_check_mark:
